recommendations.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
recommendations.description: Resources are blocking the first paint of your page. Consider delivering critical JS/CSS inline and deferring all non-critical JS/styles. Learn how to eliminate render-blocking resources.

recommendations.title: Properly size images
recommendations.description: Serve images that are appropriately-sized to save cellular data and improve load time. Learn how to size images.

recommendations.title: Minify JavaScript
recommendations.description: Minifying JavaScript files can reduce payload sizes and script parse time. Learn how to minify JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused CSS
recommendations.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused CSS.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
recommendations.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Serve images in next-gen formats
recommendations.description: Image formats like WebP and AVIF often provide better compression than PNG or JPEG, which means faster downloads and less data consumption. Learn more about modern image formats.

recommendations.title: Reduce JavaScript execution time
recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to reduce Javascript execution time.

recommendations.title: Minimize main-thread work
recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to minimize main-thread work

recommendations.title: Reduce the impact of third-party code
recommendations.description: Third-party code can significantly impact load performance. Limit the number of redundant third-party providers and try to load third-party code after your page has primarily finished loading. Learn how to minimize third-party impact.

aiSummaries.text:
**Site Analysis — Crawl Summary**  
- **Key Finding**: The website has only 2 crawlable pages, which is unusually low for a typical site.  
- **Risk**: Such a small number of pages may indicate missing content, broken links, or crawlability issues, potentially harming SEO and user experience.  
- **Action Needed**: Investigate why only 2 pages were crawled. Check for robots.txt restrictions, noindex tags, or technical errors blocking access to other pages.
aiSummaries.html:
Site Analysis — Crawl Summary

  • Key Finding: The website has only 2 crawlable pages, which is unusually low for a typical site.
  • Risk: Such a small number of pages may indicate missing content, broken links, or crawlability issues, potentially harming SEO and user experience.
  • Action Needed: Investigate why only 2 pages were crawled. Check for robots.txt restrictions, noindex tags, or technical errors blocking access to other pages.

aiSummaries.text:
**Summary of Broken Link Scan Results:**

- **All Tested Pages Affected:** Both pages scanned on the website contain broken links, indicating a widespread issue.  
- **Key Broken Links:** The same two links are broken across both pages:  
  1. **Facebook Link (400 Error):** The Facebook page link is not working, likely due to a removed or inaccessible page.  
  2. **Internal XMLRPC Link (405 Error):** An internal link is returning a "Method Not Allowed" error, suggesting a server misconfiguration or unnecessary exposure of this endpoint.  
- **Immediate Action Needed:** Fix the Facebook link to restore social media connectivity and remove or secure the `/xmlrpc.php` endpoint to prevent potential security risks or user confusion.  
- **Risk:** Broken links harm user experience and may negatively impact SEO and credibility. Prioritize resolving these issues promptly.

aiSummaries.text:
**Summary of Site Analysis — Page Performance Scan:**

- **Mobile Performance is Critically Low:** The average mobile score is 31, indicating significant performance issues that could negatively impact user experience and SEO rankings. The worst-performing page on mobile takes over 19 seconds to load its largest content, which is far beyond acceptable standards.  
- **Desktop Performance is Strong:** The average desktop score is 81, showing that the site performs well on larger devices, though there’s room for minor improvements.  
- **Key Action Items:**  
  1. **Eliminate render-blocking resources** (affecting 4 pages) to drastically reduce load times, especially on mobile.  
  2. **Optimize images** (e.g., proper sizing, deferring offscreen images) to save significant data and improve speed.  
  3. **Reduce unused CSS and minify JavaScript/CSS** to streamline page delivery.  
- **Risks:** Poor mobile performance may lead to higher bounce rates, lower conversions, and reduced search engine visibility. Prioritizing mobile optimizations is critical.  
- **Next Steps:** Focus on implementing the recommended changes for the worst-scoring pages to quickly improve overall site performance.
